newsitem.title: USA: Mass. proposes regulations for marijuana use.
newsitem.headline: Mass. proposes regulations for marijuana use.

text.p: Massachusetts proposed regulations Tuesday that would implement a law passed last year that allows patients suffering from a narrow range of medical conditions to use marijuana legally.

The state law is designed to protect patients who are certified by the state to use the drug for medical purposes from facing criminal prosecution, said Nancy Ridley, assistant commissioner of the state Department of Public Health.

The law directly challenges the Clinton administration and attempts to circumvent a threat by drug policy chief Gen. Barry McCaffrey to strip doctors of their licenses and to prosecute them if they prescribe marijuana to patients.

Unlike initiatives in California and Arizona, the Massachusetts proposal called for a three-doctor panel appointed by the public health department to screen patient applications for certification to use marijuana.
Only patients suffering from glaucoma, asthma or nausea associated with cancer treatments would be certified, Ridley said.

California voters approved a ballot measure in November that would allow sick people and their "primary care-giver" to legally grow and possess marijuana when recommended by a doctor. Arizona voters approved a similiar measure in November.

Massachusetts health officials hope to establish a research programme to study the efficacy of marijuana in treatments and to gain the cooperation of federal authorities to receive the necessary amounts of federally grown marijuana, Ridley said.
The proposals are a preliminary steps to a public hearing next month and final approval in March or April, she said.
"We're taking the first steps in identifying patients who are eligible for admission to the clinical trial," she said. "It's not like a passport to go out on the street and buy marijuana."
